content.key_idea: Prior single-level stores (EROS, Aurora) split volatile runtime/DRAM caches from disk-based backups and need extra consistency machinery, while TreeSLS collapses memory and storage into one NVM tier with a hierarchy-aware backup.

summary: This figure compares the memory/storage architectures of two prior single-level stores, EROS and Aurora, against TreeSLS, the paper's own whole-system persistent microkernel. All three columns share a process cache row, but EROS and Aurora keep a separate DRAM object cache and a disk-based backup split into inconsistent and consistent copies (checkpoint area/home location for EROS, inconsistent/consistent backup for Aurora), reflecting their two-tiered runtime-memory-plus-disk design. TreeSLS instead merges memory and storage into a single NVM tier, replacing the DRAM cache with a unified 'recoverable state and cache' box and replacing the disk row with a 'runtime' and 'backup (with hierarchy)' pair of NVM regions, connected by small icons showing that a hierarchy child can be tracked as NULL. The comparison argues that TreeSLS avoids the extra caching and consistency machinery the two-tiered prior systems require.
summary_zh: 该图以矩阵形式对比 EROS、Aurora 与 TreeSLS 的缓存/内存/存储层次：前两者在易失内存与磁盘备份间需要额外一致性机制，而 TreeSLS 用单一 NVM 层统一运行时与备份，并支持层级化、可含 NULL 子节点的备份。
